page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. This x86_64 architecture system features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, and does not include local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark results show strong performance across multiple categories. The server ranks in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by CPU flags such as AVX-512 and AES, reflected in strong Passmark encryption and extended instruction scores. Memory performance is mixed, with read-only small block bandwidth in the top 25%, while large block read-only bandwidth and Passmark memory scores fall into the middle 50% average tier.

For database and key-value store operations, the server demonstrates strong capabilities, achieving 67.43 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and ranking in the top 25% for Passmark database operations. Large language model (LLM) inference speeds are highly variable; prompt processing for a small 135M model reaches top-tier performance in the top 10%, whereas text generation for larger 70B models drops to average performance. The absence of local storage means all storage must be network-attached, which is a key architectural tradeoff.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU, leveraging DDR5 memory and dedicated AMD EPYC cores to deliver strong compute-per-resource value without the overhead of hyperthreading. This profile makes the server suitable for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks.
